title: TLS verification disabled ({lang}) — review required
description: Certificate or hostname verification is switched off in {lang}: {sink}. The connection then trusts any certificate, so an active attacker intercepts credentials, tokens, and data. This lexical rule flags the switch; the reviewer confirms it is test-only or restores verification.
remediation: Delete the switch and verify against the system store ({safe}); for private CAs, pin the CA instead of disabling checks.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the switch regardless of environment. Per-client verify=False forms are separate rules.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on TLS-disabling settings in {lang} code or config.
fp: Local test harnesses against self-signed fixtures are the common false positive — confirm test scope.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} disables a TLS authenticity check. Without verification, encryption still runs but against whoever answers — including an attacker. The remedy is restoring verification ({safe}).
applicability: {lang} TLS clients and configuration; single-line lexical scope.
risk: Machine-in-the-middle interception of all traffic on the connection; HIGH severity.
why: {lang} TLS verification is disabled ({sink}), so any certificate is trusted.
fix: Remove the switch and verify with {safe}.
For private CAs, configure the CA bundle explicitly.
Re-run the scan and confirm no disabling switch remains outside tests.
verifyT: Rescan shows no disabling switch outside tests, and invalid certificates are refused.

go: system roots plus private CA pool

title: Debug mode enabled ({lang}) — review required
description: Debug behavior is switched on in {lang}: {sink}. Debug modes expose tracebacks, consoles, or verbose errors to whoever can reach the service. This lexical rule flags the switch; the reviewer confirms it is local-only or turns it off.
remediation: Gate the switch on {safe} and default it off.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the switch regardless of environment. Generic debug=true forms are separate rules.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on debug-enabling settings in {lang} code or config.
fp: Local development configuration is the common false positive — confirm it cannot ship.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} enables debug behavior. Debug output and consoles turn minor flaws into disclosure or execution. The remedy is environment gating via {safe}.
risk: Information disclosure and debug-console execution; MEDIUM severity, HIGH when public.
why: {lang} debug mode is enabled ({sink}), exposing internals to whoever reaches the service.
fix: Gate the switch with {safe}, defaulting off.
Fail startup when debug is on outside development.
Re-run the scan and confirm no debug switch remains enabled.
verifyT: Rescan shows no enabled debug switch, and production starts with debug off.

title: Overly open CORS ({lang}) — review required
description: Cross-origin sharing in {lang} is opened wide: {sink}. Any site can then read responses with the victim's ambient credentials where credentials are allowed, or probe APIs otherwise. This lexical rule flags the opening; the reviewer confirms the scope or narrows it.
remediation: List exact trusted origins ({safe}) and avoid credentials with wildcards.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches open CORS regardless of credential settings. Framework allow_origins forms are separate rules.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on open CORS settings in {lang} code or config.
fp: Public, unauthenticated APIs intentionally open are the common accepted case.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} lets foreign origins read responses. Wildcard origins combine dangerously with credentialed requests. The remedy is an explicit origin list ({safe}).
applicability: {lang} API servers and middleware; single-line lexical scope.
risk: Cross-origin data theft where credentials apply; MEDIUM severity.
why: {lang} CORS is opened wide ({sink}), letting foreign sites read responses.
fix: Never combine wildcard origins with credentials.
Re-run the scan and confirm no open CORS remains on sensitive APIs.
verifyT: Rescan shows no open CORS on sensitive APIs, and foreign origins are refused.

title: Secret in a framework or file context ({lang}) — review required
description: A secret is embedded in a {lang} context: {sink}. Context-shaped secrets (framework keys, connection strings, config values) ship to checkouts and artifacts like any hardcoded value. This lexical rule flags the embedding; the reviewer confirms it is a placeholder or externalizes it.
remediation: Load the value from {safe} and rotate the embedded one.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches embedded values regardless of liveness. Generic secret assignments are separate rules.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on context-embedded secrets in {lang} code or config.
fp: Placeholder-shaped values (changeme, xxx) are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} places a secret where the framework or file format expects it. Context does not protect the value: it still lands in history, images, and dumps. The remedy is external storage via {safe}.
applicability: {lang} framework settings, connection strings, and config files; single-line lexical scope.
risk: Credential exposure through checkouts and artifacts; HIGH severity when the value is live.
why: {lang} contexts embed secret values ({sink}), which leak through history and artifacts.
fix: Move the value to {safe} and reference it.
Re-run the scan and confirm no embedded secret remains.
verifyT: Rescan shows no embedded secret, and rotation is complete.

universal: integrated auth or a secret store
shell: the process environment, never the file
ini: a secret include outside version control

title: Insecure Django setting ({lang}) — review required
description: A Django security setting is left open: {sink}. Django's secure defaults exist to be switched on for deployment; the open value weakens host validation, transport, or cookie handling. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer confirms local-only scope or hardens it.
remediation: Set the deployment value ({safe}) outside local settings.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the setting regardless of settings module.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on insecure Django settings in {lang} code.
fp: Local-only settings modules are the common false positive — confirm they cannot deploy.
recordDesc: In Django, {sink} keeps a protection off. Host validation, HTTPS redirect, and secure cookie flags each close a real attack path. The remedy is the deployment value ({safe}).
risk: Host-spoofing, downgrade, or cookie theft depending on the setting; MEDIUM severity.
why: Django security settings stay open ({sink}), weakening deployment protections.
fix: Split local and deployment settings so the open value cannot ship.
Re-run the scan and confirm no open setting remains deployable.
verifyT: Rescan shows no open setting deployable, and deployment checks pass.
